### First Law of Thermodynamics
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, but can only be converted from one form to another. For a closed system, $\Delta U = Q - W$ (where $Q$ is heat added, $W$ is work done, and $\Delta U$ is change in internal energy).
* *Example:* Heating water in a closed kettle where electrical energy converts into thermal energy.

### Second Law of Thermodynamics
It is impossible for a self-acting machine, unaided by any external agency, to transfer heat from a cooler body to a hotter body (Clausius statement), or convert all heat absorbed from a thermal reservoir into work without rejecting some heat to a lower temperature sink (Kelvin-Planck statement).
* *Example:* Heat naturally flows from a hot coffee cup to the colder surrounding air, but never spontaneously flows back.
